why: This fixture exists to test one claim: that an LLM can orchestrate primitives
against Minecraft's geometry, rather than route a sentence to a pre-written
procedure. 152 commands are registered and 98 describe themselves as
multi-step. If the bot only passes with those available, it is a router.
The task is 'go get some wood and make me some charcoal'. Charcoal needs a
furnace; a furnace needs 8 cobblestone; cobblestone needs a pickaxe; a pickaxe
needs planks and sticks. Nothing tells the bot that chain. Deriving it IS the
test, which is why allowed_commands below excludes every command that would
make a sequencing decision in JavaScript -- especially !prepareWoodenTool,
which performs the exact dependency step being measured.
Forest biome with features enabled, so real trees generate on flat ground.
Stone sits in the layer stack for cobblestone. Surface is y=100 like the
deliver fixture, and dry land runs in every direction.

orchestration.principle: mechanics are allowed, sequencing is not

deliberately_excluded.!requestItemGoal: goal-director runs the whole acquire-and-deliver chain
deliberately_excluded.!assignMiningJob / !assignHarvestJob / !: persistent quotas with tool preparation and delivery built in
deliberately_excluded.!addToAgenda / agenda commands: sequencing lane; the LLM must hold the sequence
deliberately_excluded.!prepareWoodenTool: survival-bootstraps the tool dependency -- the exact reasoning step under test
deliberately_excluded.!collectWood: resolves 'wood' to any log type; the bot should name the block it wants
deliberately_excluded.!newAction: writes JavaScript. A pass would prove code generation, not orchestration. Already blocked unless allow_insecure_coding.
